strengths: Well-motivated problem: Comprehensive error analysis establishing that 67% of multimodal reasoning failures stem from perception rather than reasoning failures
Practical simplicity: PAPO is a straightforward modification to GRPO/DAPO requiring no additional data, reward models, or teacher models
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Consistent improvements (4.4%-17.5% overall, 8.0%-19.1% on vision-dependent tasks) across 8 benchmarks with multiple model sizes and variants
Careful treatment of failure modes: Identifies KLprcp Hacking, proposes principled regularization via Double Entropy Loss with thorough analysis of contributing factors
Excellent reproducibility: Code provided, detailed implementation details, extensive supplementary experiments, clear hyperparameter specifications
Strong practical results: 30.5% reduction in perception errors with vision-dependency analysis showing expected behavior
Well-executed presentation: Clear motivation, good figures, logical organization, and transparent discussion of limitations
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: Using visual masking and KL divergence for perception grounding is intuitive but not particularly novel; contribution is primarily in application and engineering rather than methodological innovation

Concerning training stability: Severe hyperparameter sensitivity (γ=0.02 causes collapse on 7B but not 3B; γ=0.04 causes failure) and need for Double Entropy Loss regularization suggest fundamental instability, limiting practical applicability to new models

Incomplete mechanism understanding: Only 41% of original perception errors fully corrected; 24% remain perception errors, 25% shift to other error types (Figure 15), suggesting mechanism is more complex than presented

Limited evaluation scope: Only tested on Qwen models (acknowledged limitation); all benchmarks are small-scale reasoning tasks; unclear if 67% perception error finding and approach generalize to other vision-language tasks or model families

Counterintuitive masking findings: Random masking outperforming semantic-aware masking lacks strong theoretical justification; 60% masking ratio is aggressive and unclear if truly 'corrupting' vs. removing most information

Weak theoretical grounding: Why should maximizing KL(π_θ || π_masked) specifically improve perception? Information gain perspective is intuitive but not rigorously justified; no clear explanation for why this is preferable to alternatives

Missing statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; unclear if results average over multiple runs; some improvements relatively modest (1.53% on Qwen2.5-VL-7B general reasoning)
Incomplete baseline comparisons: Limited direct comparison with other perception-focused methods; no ablation against simpler alternatives like attention penalties
Computational overhead: ~14-19% increase in training time compounds over long training runs, limiting adoption despite authors' acknowledgment
Hyperparameter complexity: Multiple hyperparameters (γ, η₁, η₂) require different tuning for different model sizes, reducing practical applicability and generalization to new settings
